name: Senegal

claims.title: Islam reaches the Senegal River
claims.summary: North African Muslim traders introduce Islam to the peoples of the Senegal valley well before any ruler adopts it officially.

sources.label: Islam Is Introduced into West Africa (750 CE)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-850-islam-reaches-the-senegal-river, claim TL:SEN:event:850:islam-reaches-the-senegal-river, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War Jabi adopts Islamic law in Takrur
claims.summary: King War Jabi of Takrur is recorded as making Sharia official, by tradition the first Sahelian ruler to do so, anchoring Islam in the region.

sources.label: Islam Is Introduced into West Africa (750 CE)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1035-war-jabi-adopts-islamic-law-in-takrur, claim TL:SEN:event:1035:war-jabi-adopts-islamic-law-in-takrur, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Takruri forces and the Almoravids
claims.summary: Takrur aligns with the Almoravid movement; black cavalry, possibly Takruri, are recorded among Almoravid forces in Iberia, reflecting Takrur's wider reach.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1086-takruri-forces-and-the-almoravids, claim TL:SEN:event:1086:takruri-forces-and-the-almoravids, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Takrur drawn into Mali's orbit
claims.summary: Political fragmentation and the rise of the Mali Empire bring Takrur under outside dynasties, ending its independent prominence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1286-takrur-drawn-into-mali-s-orbit, claim TL:SEN:event:1286:takrur-drawn-into-mali-s-orbit, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Jolof Empire
claims.summary: A Wolof confederation unites provinces between the Senegal and Gambia rivers, drawing tribute and trade across the western savanna.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1350-rise-of-the-jolof-empire, claim TL:SEN:event:1350:rise-of-the-jolof-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Guelowar dynasty in Sine and Saloum
claims.summary: The Gelwaar lineage establishes matrilineal monarchy over the Serer kingdoms of Sine and Saloum, ruling under the title Maad.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1335-guelowar-dynasty-in-sine-and-saloum, claim TL:SEN:event:1335:guelowar-dynasty-in-sine-and-saloum, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese reach the Senegambian coast
claims.summary: Portuguese ships arrive off Senegal and the Gambia, opening Atlantic maritime trade — and the first European slave raids — along the coast.

sources.label: The Roots of African Trade (World History Vol. 2)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1444-portuguese-reach-the-senegambian-coast, claim TL:SEN:event:1444:portuguese-reach-the-senegambian-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cayor breaks from Jolof
claims.summary: The coastal province of Cayor rebels and wins independence, and Baol and Waalo follow, fracturing the empire into rival kingdoms.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1556-cayor-breaks-from-jolof, claim TL:SEN:event:1556:cayor-breaks-from-jolof, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France founds Saint-Louis
claims.summary: French traders establish Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River, the first permanent French settlement and future colonial capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1659-france-founds-saint-louis, claim TL:SEN:event:1659:france-founds-saint-louis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France takes Gorée
claims.summary: France captures Gorée island from the Dutch during the Franco-Dutch War, holding the slaving and trading post for nearly three centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1677-france-takes-goree, claim TL:SEN:event:1677:france-takes-goree, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: House of Slaves built on Gorée
claims.summary: The Maison des Esclaves is constructed on Gorée; it later becomes a museum and a contested memorial to the Atlantic slave trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1776-house-of-slaves-built-on-goree, claim TL:SEN:event:1776:house-of-slaves-built-on-goree, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Citizenship granted to coastal towns
claims.summary: The French Second Republic extends citizenship to inhabitants of the coastal communes, a status later restricted before being reaffirmed in 1916.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1848-citizenship-granted-to-coastal-towns, claim TL:SEN:event:1848:citizenship-granted-to-coastal-towns, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Faidherbe begins the conquest
claims.summary: Governor Louis Faidherbe pushes up the Senegal River, conquering Waalo and building forts that subdue the interior kingdoms over decades.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1855-faidherbe-begins-the-conquest, claim TL:SEN:event:1855:faidherbe-begins-the-conquest, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Amadou Bamba founds the Mourides
claims.summary: Cheikh Amadou Bamba establishes the Mouride Sufi brotherhood, later founding the holy city of Touba in 1887 and preaching nonviolence and work.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1883-amadou-bamba-founds-the-mourides, claim TL:SEN:event:1883:amadou-bamba-founds-the-mourides, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bamba exiled; French West Africa formed
claims.summary: France exiles Amadou Bamba to Gabon for his independent influence; the same year Senegal is incorporated into French West Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1895-bamba-exiled-french-west-africa-formed, claim TL:SEN:event:1895:bamba-exiled-french-west-africa-formed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Blaise Diagne elected to the French parliament
claims.summary: Diagne becomes the first African deputy in the French National Assembly, representing the Four Communes.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1914-blaise-diagne-elected-to-the-french-parliament, claim TL:SEN:event:1914:blaise-diagne-elected-to-the-french-parliament, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Diagne Law confirms citizenship
claims.summary: Diagne secures a law affirming the originaires of the Four Communes as full French citizens who may retain Muslim personal status.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1916-the-diagne-law-confirms-citizenship, claim TL:SEN:event:1916:the-diagne-law-confirms-citizenship, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mali Federation formed
claims.summary: Senegal and the Sudanese Republic unite in the Mali Federation, seeking a federal path out of French rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1959-mali-federation-formed, claim TL:SEN:event:1959:mali-federation-formed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence within the Mali Federation
claims.summary: France grants the Mali Federation independence, transferring power on 4 April 1960; full independence follows on 20 June.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-within-the-mali-federation, claim TL:SEN:event:1960:independence-within-the-mali-federation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Senegal proclaims separate independence
claims.summary: After the federation collapses, Senegal secedes and proclaims its own independence; Senghor is elected first president.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1960-senegal-proclaims-separate-independence, claim TL:SEN:event:1960:senegal-proclaims-separate-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Senghor resigns peacefully
claims.summary: Senghor voluntarily hands power to Prime Minister Abdou Diouf, Senegal's first orderly transfer of power.

sources.label: Senegal — The Global State of Democracy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1980-senghor-resigns-peacefully, claim TL:SEN:event:1980:senghor-resigns-peacefully, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Casamance insurgency begins
claims.summary: Clashes in Ziguinchor over a Casamance flag mark the start of the MFDC separatist conflict, one of Africa's longest-running.

sources.label: Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-1982-casamance-insurgency-begins, claim TL:SEN:event:1982:casamance-insurgency-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wade defeats Diouf
claims.summary: Abdoulaye Wade wins the presidency from Abdou Diouf — Senegal's first transfer of power across party lines.

sources.label: Senegal — The Global State of Democracy
Senegal's Democratic Evolution: Elections, Governance, and Presidential Legacies
sources.publisher: Centre for Democracy and Development Africa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-2000-wade-defeats-diouf, claim TL:SEN:event:2000:wade-defeats-diouf, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Macky Sall elected
claims.summary: Sall defeats Wade at the polls, continuing Senegal's pattern of competitive elections and peaceful handovers.

sources.label: Senegal's Democratic Evolution: Elections, Governance, and Presidential Legacies
sources.publisher: Centre for Democracy and Development Africa

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-2012-macky-sall-elected, claim TL:SEN:event:2012:macky-sall-elected, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Casamance peace agreement
claims.summary: A peace deal between the government and MFDC factions proves more durable than earlier ceasefires; violence drops sharply.

sources.label: Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-2022-casamance-peace-agreement, claim TL:SEN:event:2022:casamance-peace-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Faye wins after democratic crisis
claims.summary: After Macky Sall's attempt to delay the election is overturned, Bassirou Diomaye Faye wins; power passes peacefully again.

sources.label: Senegal — The Global State of Democracy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Senegal: From Takrur to a poet's republic", terralore.co/country/SEN/chronicle#ev-2024-faye-wins-after-democratic-crisis, claim TL:SEN:event:2024:faye-wins-after-democratic-crisis, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
